scenario: AITA for telling my mom she was a bad mother? | So this is kind of a two part thing. A while back, I made my mother upset because of a couple different things I said while out with her. She was saying something about how she didn't believe in doctors and that my siblings literally beg her to go and she still puts off taking them as long as possible. I told her that's not okay, that she did that to me and I nearly died (I was hospitalized for weeks, and spent several months on bedrest recovering), and that if she keeps that up one of us really might die some day because of her. She didn't take that too well, but ended up dropping it and brushing it off as no big deal. Later on, she asked me to go grab her a drink and when I asked her what she wanted she said "well you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" And I told her no, I do not know what you like, my grandparents raised me, I still don't know anything about you. She got upset and started crying and said "what's your problem!? This is the second time today that you've been mean to me and tried to make me seem like a bad person!" I told her I'm not trying to be mean I was just saying it's not cool to not take your kid to the doctor and that I'm not going to know anything about her since I didnt grow up with her. We ended up going home shortly after and went out again the other night, a few weeks later. Well I got my brother a phone because they kept taking his (that a different family member pays for) and I wanted him to have his own, so I made it clear they can keep his other one and this one is STRICTLY for him. Well I found out they've been taking and using this one too, so when I saw her I told her, seriously, I dont want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished for what you're doing, but I will take it back if you don't stop stealing it from him. She got upset and starting yelling and crying saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her well to be honest she kind of IS one. She had a meltdown and started sobbing and said well fine, I don't need you in my life anyways, and left without me. Now my family is saying I shouldn't of treated her like that even if she wasn't that great to me. AITA?

Then, later, she asked me to get her a drink and said something like, "You should know what I like, I've raised you for 26 years." I responded that I don't know because my grandparents raised me, so I don't know anything about her. She got upset and cried, saying I was trying to make her seem bad. I tried to explain I wasn't being mean, just pointing out her actions weren't cool. We went home, and a few weeks later, we went out again. I gave my brother a phone, but they kept taking his other phone, which someone else pays for. I made it clear this new phone was strictly for him. But I found out they were taking that one too. I told her I don't want to take it back because I don't want him punished, but I will if she doesn't stop. She got upset, yelling and crying, saying I shouldn't treat her like a bad mother. I told her honestly she kind of is. She had a meltdown, said she doesn't need me in her life, and left. Now, my family is saying I shouldn't have treated her like that, even if she wasn't great to me. So, AITA? Should I have done that? First, I need to consider the dynamics here. Then, when I tried to get her a drink, she made a comment that implied I should know her preferences, which I don't because I was raised by my grandparents. That led to a confrontation where I told her I don't know her, which upset her. Later, with the phone issue, she continued taking things that aren't hers, and I set a boundary. She reacted by saying I shouldn't treat her like a bad mother, and I told her she kind of is. That led to her leaving and my family reproaching me. So, is it right or wrong to tell my mom she's a bad mother? Let's break it down. On one hand, I'm standing up for myself and my brother. My health was at risk because of her actions, and she didn't take responsibility. The phone issue shows a pattern of taking things that aren't hers, which is another form of neglect or irresponsibility. Setting boundaries is important, but maybe the way I did it was harsh. On the other hand, calling her a bad mother directly could be seen as hurtful, even if it's true. It might have escalated the situation, leading to her leaving and family tension. Maybe there's a better way to communicate my feelings without labeling her. I also need to consider the impact on my family. My family is saying I shouldn't have treated her like that, which suggests they either don't see her actions as bad or they value the family relationship more. But I feel justified because of the harm she's caused. Perhaps I should have communicated my concerns without directly calling her a bad mother. Using "I" statements to express how her actions affect me might have been more effective. For example, saying, "I feel hurt when you don't take us to the doctor because it affects my health," instead of blaming her. Also, setting boundaries is important, but maybe in a more constructive way. Instead of telling her she's a bad mother, I could have explained how her actions impact our relationship and set clear expectations without the label. In the end, while my intentions were to protect myself and my brother, the way I expressed it might have been too direct and hurtful, leading to a breakdown in communication. It's possible that a different approach could have addressed the issues without causing such conflict.
